Telco Customer Churn Classification¶

Predict customer churn from service, billing and customer attributes. F1 is the primary selection metric; the saved Logistic Regression model achieved test F1 of 0.711 at a development-selected threshold of 0.353.

Public repository scope¶

Source datasets and row-level exports remain local. See ../data/README.md for acquisition, exclusions and replay limits. Saved aggregate results and useful figures are retained; private row previews and machine paths have been omitted from display outputs.

Project Objective¶

Identify customers at higher risk of churn so retention teams can prioritize outreach. The target is Churn, with Yes as the positive class. Predictive associations can guide review but do not establish why a customer leaves.

Evaluation Metrics¶

Churn is the minority class, so F1 score is the primary model-selection metric. F1 balances precision and recall while giving the minority churn class more attention than accuracy alone.

  • Precision: Of customers predicted to churn, the proportion who actually churned.
  • Recall: Of customers who actually churned, the proportion identified by the model.
  • F1 score: The harmonic mean of precision and recall.
  • ROC-AUC: The model's ability to rank churners above non-churners across all possible thresholds.
  • Average Precision (AP): Precision-recall performance across thresholds, which is especially informative for an imbalanced target.

Accuracy is included for context but is not the primary metric because a model can achieve misleadingly high accuracy by favoring the majority non-churn class.

Analytical Approach¶

Compare five model families using training and validation data, then select a model and F1 threshold from five-fold out-of-fold development predictions. Evaluate the locked choices on the test partition and interpret the selected model. The reserve partition stays unused.

The threshold reflects F1, not retention costs or team capacity. Those operational tradeoffs require separate assessment.

Libraries and Setup¶

Use the pinned requirements and run cells in order. This notebook performs training and replaces generated tables, figures and the final model when rerun. Random state 42 controls the splits and stochastic estimators.

Scikit-learn pipelines fit preprocessing within training folds. CatBoost handles categories directly, and SHAP supports interpretation of the selected model.

def find_project_root(filename: str) -> Path:
    start = Path.cwd().resolve()
    for candidate in [start, *start.parents]:
        if (candidate / "data" / filename).exists():
            return candidate
    raise FileNotFoundError(
        f"Could not find data/{filename} from {start}. "
        "Place the CSV in the project data directory."
    )

Dataset Overview and Data Cleaning¶

Cleaning happens before exploration or model work. Text fields are standardized, blank text is treated as missing, exact duplicates are removed, duplicate customer IDs are rejected, and the target is checked for valid Yes and No labels.

Source missingness is documented rather than solved globally. Imputation occurs only inside the relevant model-training pipeline so validation and test values cannot leak into feature preparation.

In [3]:
REQUIRED_COLUMNS = {"customerID", "Churn"}


def normalise_text_columns(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    result = frame.copy()
    for column in result.select_dtypes(include=["object", "string"]):
        result[column] = result[column].astype("string").str.strip()
        result[column] = result[column].replace({"": pd.NA})
    return result


def clean_source(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    cleaned = frame.copy()
    cleaned.columns = cleaned.columns.str.strip()
    missing_required = REQUIRED_COLUMNS.difference(cleaned.columns)
    if missing_required:
        raise ValueError(f"Missing required columns: {sorted(missing_required)}")
    cleaned = normalise_text_columns(cleaned)
    permitted_targets = {"Yes", "No"}
    observed_targets = set(cleaned["Churn"].dropna().unique())
    invalid_targets = observed_targets.difference(permitted_targets)
    if cleaned["Churn"].isna().any() or invalid_targets:
        raise ValueError(
            "Churn must contain only complete Yes/No values. "
            f"Unexpected values: {sorted(invalid_targets)}"
        )
    duplicate_rows = int(cleaned.duplicated().sum())
    cleaned = cleaned.drop_duplicates().copy()
    duplicate_customer_ids = int(cleaned["customerID"].duplicated().sum())
    if duplicate_customer_ids:
        raise ValueError(
            "customerID must be unique after exact duplicate removal. "
            f"Found {duplicate_customer_ids} duplicate IDs."
        )
    audit = pd.DataFrame(
        [
            {
                "Source rows": len(frame),
                "Exact duplicates removed": duplicate_rows,
                "Rows after cleaning": len(cleaned),
                "Duplicate customer IDs": duplicate_customer_ids,
                "Columns": cleaned.shape[1],
            }
        ]
    )
    return cleaned, audit

Feature Types and Feature Engineering¶

customerID is retained only for audit and scoring exports. contract_end_date is checked as a date and excluded from the model; days_to_renewal provides the relative timing input. Its availability before churn still needs source verification.

Five row-level features summarize ticket escalation, friction events, reliability events, log tenure and monthly charges relative to tenure. They use only fields from the same customer row; learned transformations remain in the training pipelines.

In [8]:
def build_feature_frame(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    required_inputs = {
        "tenure",
        "MonthlyCharges",
        "support_tickets_30d",
        "support_tickets_90d",
        "complaints_90d",
        "late_payments_6m",
        "billing_disputes_6m",
        "plan_downgrade_90d",
        "dropped_calls_30d",
        "area_outages_90d",
        "contract_end_date",
    }
    missing_inputs = required_inputs.difference(frame.columns)
    if missing_inputs:
        raise ValueError(f"Missing feature inputs: {sorted(missing_inputs)}")

    features = normalise_text_columns(frame).drop(
        columns=["Churn", "customerID"], errors="ignore"
    )
    contract_end = pd.to_datetime(features["contract_end_date"], errors="coerce")
    invalid_dates = (
        contract_end.isna().sum() - features["contract_end_date"].isna().sum()
    )
    if invalid_dates:
        raise ValueError(f"Found {invalid_dates} invalid contract_end_date values")
    features = features.drop(columns="contract_end_date")

    features["support_ticket_escalation"] = (
        features["support_tickets_30d"] - features["support_tickets_90d"] / 3
    )
    features["customer_friction_events"] = (
        features["complaints_90d"]
        + features["late_payments_6m"]
        + features["billing_disputes_6m"]
        + features["plan_downgrade_90d"]
    )
    features["service_reliability_events"] = (
        features["dropped_calls_30d"] + features["area_outages_90d"]
    )
    features["tenure_log"] = np.log1p(features["tenure"])
    features["monthly_charge_per_tenure"] = features["MonthlyCharges"] / (
        features["tenure"] + 1
    )
    return features

Data Preparation and Partitioning¶

The split uses stratification so the churn rate remains comparable across sets:

  • Training: 40%
  • Validation: 20%
  • Test: 20%
  • Reserve: 20%

The test set is reserved for final evaluation. It must not be used to select features, tune hyperparameters, or choose the classification threshold.

Preprocessing Pipeline and Validation Utilities¶

Each candidate model receives fold-safe preparation. Logistic Regression uses standardized numeric values; Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM use median numeric imputation with missingness indicators plus one-hot categorical encoding. CatBoost uses native categorical handling and numeric missing values.

For every hyperparameter configuration, the decision threshold is selected on validation probabilities to maximise F1. No test labels influence tuning.

In [10]:
def catboost_input(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    result = frame.copy()
    for column in categorical_columns:
        result[column] = result[column].astype("string").fillna("Missing")
    return result


def make_preprocessor(
    feature_frame: pd.DataFrame, scale_numeric: bool
) -> ColumnTransformer:
    numeric = feature_frame.select_dtypes(include=np.number).columns.tolist()
    categorical = feature_frame.select_dtypes(exclude=np.number).columns.tolist()
    numeric_steps = [("impute", SimpleImputer(strategy="median", add_indicator=True))]
    if scale_numeric:
        numeric_steps.append(("scale", StandardScaler()))
    return ColumnTransformer(
        transformers=[
            ("numeric", Pipeline(steps=numeric_steps), numeric),
            (
                "categorical",
                Pipeline(
                    steps=[
                        ("impute", SimpleImputer(strategy="most_frequent")),
                        ("encode", OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore")),
                    ]
                ),
                categorical,
            ),
        ],
        verbose_feature_names_out=False,
    )

def make_model(model_name: str, parameters: dict, X_fit: pd.DataFrame):
    if model_name == "Logistic Regression":
        return Pipeline(
            steps=[
                ("preprocess", make_preprocessor(X_fit, scale_numeric=True)),
                (
                    "model",
                    LogisticRegression(
                        C=parameters["C"],
                        max_iter=4000,
                        random_state=RANDOM_STATE,
                    ),
                ),
            ]
        )
    if model_name == "Random Forest":
        return Pipeline(
            steps=[
                ("preprocess", make_preprocessor(X_fit, scale_numeric=False)),
                (
                    "model",
                    RandomForestClassifier(
                        n_estimators=350,
                        class_weight="balanced_subsample",
                        random_state=RANDOM_STATE,
                        n_jobs=-1,
                        **parameters,
                    ),
                ),
            ]
        )
    if model_name == "XGBoost":
        return Pipeline(
            steps=[
                ("preprocess", make_preprocessor(X_fit, scale_numeric=False)),
                (
                    "model",
                    XGBClassifier(
                        objective="binary:logistic",
                        eval_metric="logloss",
                        subsample=0.9,
                        colsample_bytree=0.9,
                        reg_lambda=5.0,
                        random_state=RANDOM_STATE,
                        n_jobs=-1,
                        **parameters,
                    ),
                ),
            ]
        )
    if model_name == "CatBoost":
        return CatBoostClassifier(
            loss_function="Logloss",
            random_seed=RANDOM_STATE,
            verbose=False,
            allow_writing_files=False,
            **parameters,
        )
    if model_name == "LightGBM":
        return Pipeline(
            steps=[
                ("preprocess", make_preprocessor(X_fit, scale_numeric=False)),
                (
                    "model",
                    LGBMClassifier(
                        subsample=0.9,
                        colsample_bytree=0.9,
                        reg_lambda=3.0,
                        random_state=RANDOM_STATE,
                        n_jobs=-1,
                        verbosity=-1,
                        **parameters,
                    ),
                ),
            ]
        )
    raise ValueError(f"Unknown model: {model_name}")


def fit_and_predict(model_name, parameters, X_fit, y_fit, X_predict):
    model = make_model(model_name, parameters, X_fit)
    if model_name == "CatBoost":
        model.fit(
            catboost_input(X_fit),
            y_fit,
            cat_features=categorical_columns,
        )
        probability = model.predict_proba(catboost_input(X_predict))[:, 1]
    else:
        model.fit(X_fit, y_fit)
        probability = model.predict_proba(X_predict)[:, 1]
    return probability, model


def predict_probability(model_name, model, features):
    if model_name == "CatBoost":
        return model.predict_proba(catboost_input(features))[:, 1]
    return model.predict_proba(features)[:, 1]


def find_f1_threshold(y_true, probabilities):
    thresholds = np.linspace(0.05, 0.95, 901)
    scores = [
        f1_score(y_true, probabilities >= threshold, zero_division=0)
        for threshold in thresholds
    ]
    best_index = int(np.argmax(scores))
    return float(thresholds[best_index]), float(scores[best_index])


def probability_metrics(y_true, probabilities, threshold):
    prediction = probabilities >= threshold
    return {
        "Accuracy": accuracy_score(y_true, prediction),
        "Precision": precision_score(y_true, prediction, zero_division=0),
        "Recall": recall_score(y_true, prediction, zero_division=0),
        "F1": f1_score(y_true, prediction, zero_division=0),
        "ROC-AUC": roc_auc_score(y_true, probabilities),
        "Average Precision": average_precision_score(y_true, probabilities),
    }


def save_validation_diagnostics(model_name, y_true, probabilities, threshold):
    artifact_key = safe_filename(model_name)
    prediction = probabilities >= threshold
    metrics_table = pd.DataFrame(
        [
            {
                "Threshold": threshold,
                **probability_metrics(y_true, probabilities, threshold),
            }
        ]
    )
    metrics_table.to_csv(
        TABLE_DIR / f"telco_churn_v2_{artifact_key}_validation_metrics.csv",
        index=False,
    )
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.5, 4.5))
    ConfusionMatrixDisplay.from_predictions(
        y_true,
        prediction,
        display_labels=["No churn", "Churn"],
        colorbar=False,
        ax=ax,
    )
    ax.grid(False)
    ax.set_title(f"{model_name}: validation confusion matrix")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(
        VISUALS_DIR / f"telco_churn_v2_{artifact_key}_validation_confusion_matrix.png",
        dpi=300,
        bbox_inches="tight",
        facecolor="white",
    )
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.5, 4.5))
    RocCurveDisplay.from_predictions(y_true, probabilities, ax=ax)
    ax.set_title(f"{model_name}: validation ROC curve")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(
        VISUALS_DIR / f"telco_churn_v2_{artifact_key}_validation_roc_curve.png",
        dpi=300,
        bbox_inches="tight",
        facecolor="white",
    )
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.5, 4.5))
    PrecisionRecallDisplay.from_predictions(y_true, probabilities, ax=ax)
    ax.set_title(f"{model_name}: validation precision-recall curve")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(
        VISUALS_DIR
        / f"telco_churn_v2_{artifact_key}_validation_precision_recall_curve.png",
        dpi=300,
        bbox_inches="tight",
        facecolor="white",
    )
    return metrics_table


def run_preliminary_model(model_name: str):
    records = []
    model_started = perf_counter()
    for configuration_number, parameters in enumerate(
        MODEL_CONFIGURATIONS[model_name], start=1
    ):
        candidate_started = perf_counter()
        probability, _ = fit_and_predict(
            model_name, parameters, X_train, y_train, X_validation
        )
        threshold, _ = find_f1_threshold(y_validation, probability)
        records.append(
            {
                "Candidate": f"{model_name} #{configuration_number}",
                "Model": model_name,
                "Parameters": parameters,
                "Train + validation seconds": perf_counter() - candidate_started,
                "Threshold": threshold,
                **probability_metrics(y_validation, probability, threshold),
            }
        )
    tuning_table = (
        pd.DataFrame(records)
        .sort_values(["F1", "Average Precision", "ROC-AUC"], ascending=False)
        .reset_index(drop=True)
    )
    artifact_key = safe_filename(model_name)
    tuning_export = tuning_table.copy()
    tuning_export["Parameters"] = tuning_export["Parameters"].map(json.dumps)
    tuning_export.to_csv(
        TABLE_DIR / f"telco_churn_v2_{artifact_key}_hyperparameter_tuning.csv",
        index=False,
    )
    selected = tuning_table.iloc[0]
    selected_probability, _ = fit_and_predict(
        model_name,
        selected["Parameters"],
        X_train,
        y_train,
        X_validation,
    )
    threshold_grid = np.linspace(0.05, 0.95, 901)
    threshold_table = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "Threshold": threshold_grid,
            "F1": [
                f1_score(
                    y_validation, selected_probability >= threshold, zero_division=0
                )
                for threshold in threshold_grid
            ],
        }
    )
    threshold_table.to_csv(
        TABLE_DIR / f"telco_churn_v2_{artifact_key}_threshold_tuning.csv",
        index=False,
    )
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4.5))
    ax.plot(threshold_table["Threshold"], threshold_table["F1"], color="#1b9e77")
    ax.axvline(selected["Threshold"], color="#d95f02", linestyle="--")
    ax.set_title(f"{model_name}: validation threshold tuning")
    ax.set_xlabel("Classification threshold")
    ax.set_ylabel("F1 score")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(
        VISUALS_DIR / f"telco_churn_v2_{artifact_key}_threshold_tuning.png",
        dpi=300,
        bbox_inches="tight",
        facecolor="white",
    )
    validation_metrics = save_validation_diagnostics(
        model_name,
        y_validation,
        selected_probability,
        float(selected["Threshold"]),
    )
    print(
        f"{model_name}: preliminary tuning completed in "
        f"{perf_counter() - model_started:.2f} seconds"
    )
    return tuning_table, selected, validation_metrics

Logistic Regression is an interpretable baseline. The regularisation strength C is compared on validation data, and its validation threshold is selected for F1 score.

Final Cross-Validated Model-Selection Framework¶

The preliminary tables tune each model family on the 40% training and 20% validation partitions. To make the final selection more stable, the strongest reproducible configuration for each family is then compared with five-fold stratified out-of-fold predictions from the combined 60% development data.

The test and reserve partitions remain completely excluded from this process. The threshold is selected only from the out-of-fold development probabilities.

These OOF scores support selection, rather than an independent performance estimate: preliminary choices already used development labels, and the threshold is optimized on the pooled OOF labels. The separate test metrics evaluate the resulting locked choice.

In [18]:
X_train_final = pd.concat([X_train, X_validation])
y_train_final = pd.concat([y_train, y_validation])
FINAL_CV_CONFIGURATIONS = {
    "Logistic Regression": {"C": 1.00},
    "Random Forest": {"max_depth": None, "min_samples_leaf": 3, "max_features": 0.8},
    "XGBoost": {
        "max_depth": 3,
        "min_child_weight": 5,
        "learning_rate": 0.03,
        "n_estimators": 500,
    },
    "CatBoost": {
        "depth": 5,
        "learning_rate": 0.03,
        "l2_leaf_reg": 8,
        "iterations": 500,
    },
    "LightGBM": {
        "num_leaves": 7,
        "min_child_samples": 30,
        "learning_rate": 0.025,
        "n_estimators": 500,
    },
}
cv = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=RANDOM_STATE)
final_cv_records = []
final_cv_probabilities = {}
for model_name, parameters in FINAL_CV_CONFIGURATIONS.items():
    cv_started = perf_counter()
    oof_probability = np.zeros(len(X_train_final))
    for fit_position, fold_position in cv.split(X_train_final, y_train_final):
        fold_probability, _ = fit_and_predict(
            model_name,
            parameters,
            X_train_final.iloc[fit_position],
            y_train_final.iloc[fit_position],
            X_train_final.iloc[fold_position],
        )
        oof_probability[fold_position] = fold_probability
    threshold, _ = find_f1_threshold(y_train_final, oof_probability)
    final_cv_probabilities[model_name] = oof_probability
    final_cv_records.append(
        {
            "Model": model_name,
            "Parameters": parameters,
            "Threshold": threshold,
            **probability_metrics(y_train_final, oof_probability, threshold),
            "Five-fold OOF seconds": perf_counter() - cv_started,
        }
    )
final_cv_selection = (
    pd.DataFrame(final_cv_records)
    .sort_values(["F1", "Average Precision", "ROC-AUC"], ascending=False)
    .reset_index(drop=True)
)
final_cv_export = final_cv_selection.copy()
final_cv_export["Parameters"] = final_cv_export["Parameters"].map(json.dumps)
final_cv_export.to_csv(
    TABLE_DIR / "telco_churn_v2_final_five_fold_cv_selection.csv",
    index=False,
)
selected_configuration = final_cv_selection.iloc[0]
selected_model_name = selected_configuration["Model"]
selected_parameters = selected_configuration["Parameters"]
selected_threshold = float(selected_configuration["Threshold"])
selected_oof_probability = final_cv_probabilities[selected_model_name]

Final Model Training and Holdout-Test Evaluation¶

Fit each locked model on the combined training and validation partitions and report its test diagnostics. Retrieve the selected model from these fitted models; selection remains based on development OOF results, not the test ranking. The reserve partition remains unused.

In [20]:
locked_test_models = {}
locked_test_probabilities = {}
all_models_test_records = []
for _, configuration in final_cv_selection.iterrows():
    model_name = configuration["Model"]
    parameters = configuration["Parameters"]
    threshold = float(configuration["Threshold"])
    fit_started = perf_counter()
    model = make_model(model_name, parameters, X_train_final)
    if model_name == "CatBoost":
        model.fit(
            catboost_input(X_train_final),
            y_train_final,
            cat_features=categorical_columns,
        )
    else:
        model.fit(X_train_final, y_train_final)
    fit_seconds = perf_counter() - fit_started
    scoring_started = perf_counter()
    probability = predict_probability(model_name, model, X_test)
    scoring_seconds = perf_counter() - scoring_started
    locked_test_models[model_name] = model
    locked_test_probabilities[model_name] = probability
    all_models_test_records.append(
        {
            "Model": model_name,
            "Parameters": json.dumps(parameters),
            "OOF-selected threshold": threshold,
            "Fit seconds": fit_seconds,
            "Test scoring seconds": scoring_seconds,
            **probability_metrics(y_test, probability, threshold),
        }
    )
all_models_test_metrics = (
    pd.DataFrame(all_models_test_records)
    .sort_values("F1", ascending=False)
    .reset_index(drop=True)
)
all_models_test_metrics.to_csv(
    TABLE_DIR / "telco_churn_v2_all_locked_models_test_metrics.csv",
    index=False,
)

Final Holdout-Test Results¶

The following tables and graphics report the final test result. They are diagnostics only and do not feed back into model, hyperparameter, or threshold selection.

In [22]:
test_predictions = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "customerID": df.loc[X_test.index, "customerID"],
        "actual_churn": y_test,

).sort_values("churn_probability", ascending=False)

Model Interpretation¶

The selected Logistic Regression model is described through absolute coefficients and SHAP values. Absolute coefficients rank the magnitude of encoded input weights; they do not show direction. SHAP contributions explain movement in the model's log-odds score, not a direct percentage-point change in churn probability.

The explanation sample comes from the final training data. Positive contributions raise the score and negative contributions lower it relative to the background. These are model associations, not causal effects. If a future run selects another family, the current fallback explains a separately labeled CatBoost companion, which must not be treated as an explanation of a different selected model.

In [26]:
shap_sample = X_train_final.sample(
    n=min(500, len(X_train_final)),
    random_state=RANDOM_STATE,
)
if selected_model_name == "Logistic Regression":
    interpretation_label = "Final Logistic Regression"
    final_preprocessor = final_model.named_steps["preprocess"]
    final_linear_model = final_model.named_steps["model"]
    shap_feature_names = final_preprocessor.get_feature_names_out()
    feature_importance_label = "Absolute coefficient"
    feature_importance = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "Feature": shap_feature_names,
            feature_importance_label: np.abs(final_linear_model.coef_.ravel()),
        }
    ).sort_values(feature_importance_label, ascending=False)
    shap_sample_transformed = final_preprocessor.transform(shap_sample)
    shap_background = final_preprocessor.transform(
        X_train_final.sample(n=min(100, len(X_train_final)), random_state=RANDOM_STATE)
    )
    shap_explainer = shap.LinearExplainer(final_linear_model, shap_background)
    shap_values = np.asarray(shap_explainer.shap_values(shap_sample_transformed))
    shap_sample_probability = predict_probability(
        selected_model_name, final_model, shap_sample
    )
    shap_sample_display_values = shap_sample_transformed
else:
    interpretation_label = "CatBoost companion model"
    companion_parameters = FINAL_CV_CONFIGURATIONS["CatBoost"]
    _, companion_model = fit_and_predict(
        "CatBoost",
        companion_parameters,
        X_train_final,
        y_train_final,
        X_train_final.iloc[:1],
    )
    shap_feature_names = feature_columns
    feature_importance_label = "CatBoost feature importance"
    feature_importance = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "Feature": shap_feature_names,
            feature_importance_label: companion_model.get_feature_importance(),
        }
    ).sort_values(feature_importance_label, ascending=False)
    shap_values_with_base = companion_model.get_feature_importance(
        Pool(catboost_input(shap_sample), cat_features=categorical_columns),
        type="ShapValues",
    )
    shap_values = shap_values_with_base[:, :-1]
    shap_sample_probability = predict_probability(
        "CatBoost", companion_model, shap_sample
    )
    shap_sample_display_values = shap_sample.astype(str).values
feature_importance.to_csv(
    TABLE_DIR / "telco_churn_v2_final_feature_importance.csv",
    index=False,
)

Model Packaging and Reproducibility¶

The model package stores the final fitted model, selected hyperparameters and threshold, feature columns, categorical columns, and source file name. The scoring helper applies the same feature construction and threshold to new v2 customer extracts.

In [33]:

    "model": final_model,
    "selected_model": selected_model_name,
    "parameters": selected_parameters,
    "threshold": selected_threshold,
    "feature_columns": feature_columns,
    "categorical_columns": categorical_columns,
    "source_filename": DATA_FILENAME,
}
model_path = MODELS_DIR / "telco_churn_v2_40_20_20_model.joblib"
joblib.dump(model_package, model_path)

In [34]:
def score_new_customers(new_customers: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    required_source_columns = set(df.columns).difference({"Churn", "customerID"})
    missing_source_columns = required_source_columns.difference(new_customers.columns)
    if missing_source_columns:
        raise ValueError(
            "New data is missing required v2 columns: "
            f"{sorted(missing_source_columns)}"
        )
    new_features = build_feature_frame(new_customers).reindex(columns=feature_columns)
    probability = predict_probability(selected_model_name, final_model, new_features)
    scored = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "customerID": new_customers.get(
                "customerID", pd.Series(index=new_customers.index)
            ),
            "churn_probability": probability,
            "predicted_churn": (probability >= selected_threshold).astype(int),
        },
        index=new_customers.index,
    )
    return scored.sort_values("churn_probability", ascending=False)

Conclusion and Limitations¶

The saved Logistic Regression model achieved test F1 of 0.711, precision of 0.681 and recall of 0.745 at threshold 0.353, meeting the 0.70 F1 objective on this split. These metrics describe the supplied v2 extract, not prospective retention outcomes.

Full-source EDA and repeated development comparisons limit independence claims. Confirm when support, billing, renewal and NPS fields were available relative to churn; the standard IBM dataset alone does not supply these v2 fields. Future evaluation should use newly collected customers under a declared time-based protocol.

Feature importance and SHAP describe model associations, not causal effects. Retention costs, probability calibration and performance over time remain unverified.
